title: Smart Water Metering and Control
headline: Battery-powered retrofit reader that turns existing water meters into smart meters, developed for a city-wide meter reading tender
photoAlt: SciFlair meter reader unit open, showing the sensor node board and battery pack
subtitle: A battery-powered reader that turns existing water meters into connected smart meters, with leak and tamper alerts
need: A large water utility went to tender for automated meter reading as a managed service. The supplier would own, install and operate the meters, the communications network and the head-end system, and deliver readings for a monthly charge per meter.

The first phase covered 4,100 high-volume users, with more than 200,000 homes and businesses to follow over four years. Readings had to arrive over GPRS or cloud IoT networks rather than drive-by or walk-by reading, with at least 99% of meters read every month and penalties for any meter offline for more than a few days.
Replacing every meter would have made the monthly charge uncompetitive. We needed to show that existing meters could be retrofitted reliably and cheaply enough to meet those service levels.
role: SciFlair was the design authority. We analysed the tender requirements and service levels, set them out as system requirements, then designed the reader hardware, firmware and head-end software, built the prototypes and tested them on meters in our lab and on site.
built: A retrofit reader that fits existing pulse-output water meters, so the meter itself stays in place
A low-power sensor node board in an IP67 enclosure, running for years on batteries
Our Axino communication module, so one reader design connects over GSM/GPRS, LoRa, SigFox, mesh, WiFi or Ethernet to suit each site
Readings stored on the device when the network is down and sent once it returns, protecting the monthly read rate
Alerts for leaks, continuous flow, tampering and devices that stop reporting
A head-end web application showing every meter on a live map, with consumption history, alarms and web-service interfaces to billing
Pump and valve control from the same platform, reusing our well pump control design

delivery.title: Concept
delivery.text: Turned the tender's scope and service levels into system requirements and measures of performance: monthly read rate, maximum outage, battery life, range and cost per meter.

delivery.title: Architecture
delivery.text: Chose a retrofit architecture on the Axino platform, so one reader design could serve different meter types and networks, with the head-end hosted in the cloud.

delivery.title: Design and build
delivery.text: Designed the sensor node board, firmware and enclosure, then built a batch of prototype readers.

delivery.title: Verification
delivery.text: Tested the readers on a range of meter types in our lab and on installed meters on site, verifying reading accuracy, battery drain and radio range in meter chambers.

delivery.title: Next iteration
delivery.text: Fed the results into a smaller, round meter-reader board that fits under the meter cover.
